references.venue: Proceedings of the 9th ACM SIGPLAN International Conference on Certified Programs and Proofs

references.limitation: Describes the earlier mathlib library; does not document the corpus's pinned 2026 mathlib revision.

references.title: Maintaining a Library of Formal Mathematics
references.claim_supported: Kernel acceptance is complemented by semantic linting and documentation checks for library quality; logical coherence does not settle every engineering property of a formal corpus.
references.limitation: Semantic linting here concerns elaborated declarations and metadata; it is not an automatic proof of agreement with an informal manuscript.
references.publisher_metadata_title: Maintaining a Library of Formal Mathematics

references.title: Use and Abuse of Instance Parameters in the Lean Mathematical Library
references.venue: 13th International Conference on Interactive Theorem Proving (ITP 2022)
references.claim_supported: Instance parameters and typeclass design patterns organize mathematical structures but create scaling and inheritance complications; their use alone is not an unusual innovation of this corpus.
references.limitation: The selected reference is the 2022 conference version, not the expanded 2025 journal version.
references.publisher_metadata_title: Use and Abuse of Instance Parameters in the Lean Mathematical Library

references.title: Packaging Mathematical Structures
references.venue: Theorem Proving in Higher Order Logics (TPHOLs 2009)
references.claim_supported: Dependent records, coercions and inference have long been used to package mathematical interfaces and multiple inheritance; the interesting evidence in IdentifiedBand is its specific mathematical payload and subsequent transport.
references.limitation: A Coq architecture paper; it supplies a conceptual baseline, not a claim that Lean directly implements its exact packed-class scheme.
references.publisher_metadata_title: Packaging Mathematical Structures

references.title: Abstraction boundaries and spec driven development in pure mathematics
references.venue: Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society
references.claim_supported: Abstraction boundaries and specification-based collaboration are established formalization methods. Section 5 separately addresses alignment of formal objects with informal mathematics through specifications and examples.
references.limitation: Supports the need for semantic alignment; does not certify alignment of the present corpus.
references.publisher_metadata_title: Abstraction boundaries and spec driven development in pure mathematics

references.title: LeanArchitect: Automating Blueprint Generation for Humans and AI
references.claim_supported: Blueprint metadata and automatically inferred declaration dependencies can be extracted directly from Lean code and exported to synchronized exposition.
references.limitation: The corpus's lakefile pins LeanArchitect, but that dependency alone does not show that every case study uses annotations or an exported blueprint. The arXiv record was verified; no publication venue is asserted.

references.title: Lean4Lean: Verifying a Typechecker for Lean, in Lean
references.claim_supported: Lean permits external proof checking implementations, and verification of a checker itself is a separate task with partial correctness results reported in this version.
references.limitation: Do not say all of Lean's kernel or metatheory is fully verified. This record's title differs from the first 2024 version, so cite the version explicitly.

references.title: The mathematical language AUTOMATH, its usage and some of its extensions
references.claim_supported: AUTOMATH supplies an early primary source for representing mathematics in a language admitting mechanical checking.
references.limitation: For the explicit modern phrase 'de Bruijn criterion', cite Barendregt and Wiedijk rather than claiming this paper states that wording.
references.publisher_metadata_title: The mathematical language AUTOMATH, its usage, and some of its extensions

references.title: The challenge of computer mathematics
references.venue: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A
references.claim_supported: The de Bruijn criterion emphasizes that a formal proof can be independently checked by a small program; proof production and independent checking need not share the entire trust base.
references.limitation: Independent checkability is an architectural principle, not evidence that this audit actually executed an independent kernel.
references.publisher_metadata_title: The challenge of computer mathematics

references.title: Metatheory and Reflection in Theorem Proving: A Survey and Critique
references.institution: SRI International Cambridge Computer Science Research Centre
references.claim_supported: Computational reflection and LCF-style checking are longstanding approaches to efficient verified reasoning, and they should be distinguished from logical reflection principles that extend a logic.
references.limitation: Use to frame certificates/reflection generally; neither TraceCone nor AllSeams is being claimed as a reflective decision procedure.

references.title: Formal proofs in real algebraic geometry: from ordered fields to quantifier elimination
references.claim_supported: Formal algebraic theories can validate algorithms and decision procedures by proving their mathematical correctness; certificate-based computation has substantial antecedents.
references.limitation: A Coq real-algebraic-geometry formalization; not a specific precedent for this corpus's analytic trace-ideal transport.

references.title: Comparator
references.claim_supported: Source-level comparison of theorem statements and dependent declarations, transitive axiom inspection, builtin kernel replay, and optional external kernel checking.
references.limitation: This is an independently pinned infrastructure snapshot. openai/math does not pin Comparator in the inspected challenge README or lakefile, so do not represent this as the exact checker used to produce the corpus.

references.title: Formalizing the Divergence Theorem and the Cauchy Integral Formula in Lean
references.venue: 13th International Conference on Interactive Theorem Proving (ITP 2022)
references.publisher_metadata_title: Formalizing the Divergence Theorem and the Cauchy Integral Formula in Lean
references.claim_supported: Earlier Lean work already formalizes integration-theory transport and careful regularity interfaces: a GP-integral divergence theorem is transferred to the Bochner integral, and the resulting rectangular-domain theorem yields Cauchy–Goursat without continuity assumptions on the complex derivative.
references.limitation: Its domains are rectangular boxes; it does not establish the sphere-local exact-form flux theorem or ordered differential-form representation used in the Mahler case.
references.closest_comparison: This gives a direct precedent for organizing analysis around the assumptions of an integration interface. Mahler's specific audited bridge concerns sphere-local form congruence and a cutoff extension.
references.suggested_placement: Discussion paragraph beginning 'These patterns have substantial antecedents', or the Mahler subsection's concluding comparison with established formal analysis.

references.title: Proofs of randomized algorithms in Coq
references.publisher_metadata_title: Proofs of randomized algorithms in Coq
references.year_note: The selected reference is the 2009 expanded journal article; its DOI contains 2007, and an earlier conference version appeared in 2006.
references.claim_supported: The Coq development interprets randomized programs as functionals M(A)=(A→[0,1])→[0,1], representing subprobabilities through expectations. It proves probability rules, supports general recursion, and verifies a Bernoulli sampler from coin flips.
references.limitation: This is an expectation-based denotational account, not a cost-bearing compiler theorem for the particular fixed oracle machine and tape positions inspected in CommonBases.
references.closest_comparison: The all-observables output certificate should be presented as a concrete application of established expectation semantics; its case-specific content is the connection to bounded banks and fixed-machine execution.
references.suggested_placement: CommonBases final comparison paragraph, alongside CertiCrypt/EasyCrypt; optionally the discussion's sentence about observations and output distributions.

references.title: Verified Foundations for Differential Privacy
references.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Programming Languages
references.publisher_metadata_title: Verified Foundations for Differential Privacy
references.claim_supported: SampCert verifies exact discrete samplers in Lean. Its SLang uses unnormalized mass functions; normalization promotes completed samplers to PMFs. Equal sampler distributions support substituting implementations without redoing downstream privacy proofs.
references.limitation: Section 4.1 explicitly retains external runtime definitions in the trusted computing base; the article does not supply CommonBases' inspected fixed-machine cost and physical-tape theorem.
references.closest_comparison: This is a close Lean precedent for separating executable sampling structure from distribution semantics and using equality of output laws as a downstream interface.
references.suggested_placement: CommonBases final comparison paragraph and discussion of preservation of probability laws; citation should support established sampler/distribution interfaces, not a rarity claim.
